atoms.text: This guide describes how to let the ArchiveBridge snapshot exporter write nightly database backups to the bucket dr-db-snapshots. The exporter runs under the IAM role snapshot-exporter-role in account 111122223333, which also owns the bucket. Access is granted entirely through an identity-based policy attached to that role. Create a policy with one statement that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::dr-db-snapshots/nightly/*, and attach it to the role. Add s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so the exporter can clean up interrupted uploads. Do not edit the bucket policy, which keeps its existing statements, including the explicit deny for requests that do not use TLS. Configure the exporter to upload each snapshot as a multipart object with a key such as nightly/2025-03-14/orders_dump. After attaching the policy, run a test export and confirm the object appears under the nightly/ prefix. Verify that the exporter cannot read or delete objects, since the policy grants only write actions.

This guide describes how to let the ArchiveBridge snapshot exporter write nightly database backups to the bucket dr-db-snapshots. The exporter runs under the IAM role snapshot-exporter-role in account 111122223333, which also owns the bucket. Access is granted entirely through statements in the bucket's resource-based policy. Add a statement whose Principal is arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/snapshot-exporter-role and that allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::dr-db-snapshots/nightly/*. Add a second statement with the same Principal that allows s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on the bucket ARN so the exporter can clean up interrupted uploads. Do not edit the role's identity-based policies, and keep the existing bucket policy statements, including the explicit deny for requests that do not use TLS. Configure the exporter to upload each snapshot as a multipart object with a key such as nightly/2025-03-14/orders_dump. After saving the bucket policy, run a test export and confirm the object appears under the nightly/ prefix. Verify that the exporter cannot read or delete objects, since the statements grant only write actions.

This guide covers permissions for the ArchiveBridge replication role that copies objects from prod-records-primary to prod-records-replica. Both buckets belong to account 111122223333 and reside in different regions. The grant is made only through an identity-based policy attached to the role replication-role. In that policy, allow s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the primary bucket ARN. Allow s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionAcl on arn:aws:s3:::prod-records-primary/*. Allow s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::prod-records-replica/*. Neither bucket policy is changed, so existing deny statements on both buckets stay in force. Set the trust policy of the role to allow the ArchiveBridge replication service to assume it, then enable versioning on both buckets. Upload a test object to the primary bucket and confirm that its replica appears in the destination with a replication status of COMPLETED.

This guide covers permissions for the ArchiveBridge replication role that copies objects from prod-records-primary to prod-records-replica. Both buckets belong to account 111122223333 and reside in different regions. The grant is made only through statements in each bucket's resource-based policy, naming the role replication-role as Principal. In the primary bucket policy, allow s3:GetReplicationConfiguration and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. In the same policy, allow s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication and s3:GetObjectVersionAcl on arn:aws:s3:::prod-records-primary/*. In the replica bucket policy, allow s3:ReplicateObject and s3:ReplicateDelete on arn:aws:s3:::prod-records-replica/* for arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/replication-role. The role's identity-based permissions are not changed, and existing deny statements on both buckets stay in force. Set the trust policy of the role to allow the ArchiveBridge replication service to assume it, then enable versioning on both buckets. Upload a test object to the primary bucket and confirm that its replica appears in the destination with a replication status of COMPLETED.

This guide explains how to give a recovery engineer read access to backups during a disaster recovery drill. The engineer signs in as the IAM user dr-restore-operator in account 111122223333, and the backups are in the bucket corp-backup-vault. Access is granted only by an identity-based policy attached to that user. The policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::corp-backup-vault/restore-set/*. A second statement allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with a condition limiting s3:prefix to restore-set/. The bucket policy is not modified, so no new statement is added to it. During the drill, the operator lists the restore-set/ prefix and downloads the most recent full backup archive. Confirm that an attempt to read keys outside restore-set/ returns an access denied error. Remove the policy from the user after the drill is complete.

Confirm that an attempt to read keys outside restore-set/ returns an access denied error. Remove the two statements from the bucket policy after the drill is complete.

This guide describes permissions for an on-premises file server that uploads incremental backups to the bucket site-backup-store. The ArchiveBridge agent on the server authenticates as the IAM user backup-agent-fs01 in account 111122223333. Access is granted exclusively through an identity-based policy attached to that user. The policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::site-backup-store/fs01/* only when the request header s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption equals AES256. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted to the prefix fs01/. The bucket policy is left unchanged. Store the user's access key in the agent's credential file with file mode 600. Run an initial backup job and check that each object under fs01/ reports server-side encryption as enabled. Confirm that an upload without the encryption header is rejected.

This guide covers read access for a job that verifies replicated backups by comparing checksums. The job runs as the IAM role integrity-checker-role in account 111122223333 and reads from the bucket archive-replica-west. The grant is made only in an identity-based policy attached to that role. The policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::archive-replica-west/*. It also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the job can enumerate keys. The bucket policy is not modified. The job lists objects, requests the stored SHA-256 checksum attribute of each one, and compares it with a manifest generated at the source. Schedule the job weekly and write its report to a local volume, not to the bucket. Confirm that any write attempt by the role to the bucket fails with access denied.

The job runs as the IAM role integrity-checker-role in account 111122223333 and reads from the bucket archive-replica-west. One statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::archive-replica-west/* for arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/integrity-checker-role. A second statement for the same role allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the job can enumerate keys. The role's identity-based policies are not modified. The job lists objects, requests the stored SHA-256 checksum attribute of each one, and compares it with a manifest generated at the source. Schedule the job weekly and write its report to a local volume, not to the bucket. Confirm that any write attempt by the role to the bucket fails with access denied.

This guide explains how to allow a retention cleanup job to delete expired object versions from the bucket backup-staging-east. The job runs as the IAM role retention-cleaner-role in account 111122223333. Access is granted solely by an identity-based policy attached to the role. The policy allows s3:ListBucketVersions on the bucket ARN and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::backup-staging-east/staging/*. It does not include s3:PutObject or s3:GetObject. The bucket policy is not changed, and its existing statements remain as they are. The job lists versions under staging/, selects those older than 35 days, and deletes them one by one. Run the job against a test prefix first and review the deletion log. Confirm that attempts to delete versions outside staging/ return access denied.

The role's identity-based policies are not changed, and the existing bucket policy statements remain as they are. The job lists versions under staging/, selects those older than 35 days, and deletes them one by one. Run the job against a test prefix first and review the deletion log. This guide describes how to let a scheduled job archive application configuration exports to the bucket config-archive-central. The job runsas the IAM role config-archiver-role in account 111122223333. The grant is provided only by an identity-based policy attached to this role. The policy allows s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::config-archive-central/exports/*. A condition requires the request tag retention to equal 90d, so every object carries a retention label. The bucket policy is not edited. Each run uploads a compressed export under a key such as exports/payments/2025-03-14_tar and applies the retention tag in the same request. After the first run, read the object's tag set and confirm the label is present. Verify that an upload without the tag is denied.

This guide covers access for a failover orchestrator that promotes the replica bucket during a regional outage. The orchestrator runs as the IAM role failover-orchestrator-role in account 111122223333 and works against the bucket app-data-replica. Access is granted only through an identity-based policy attached to the role. The policy allows s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket on the replica bucket and its objects. A separate statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::app-data-replica/failover-status/* so the orchestrator can record progress. The bucket policy is left unchanged. At failover, the orchestrator reads the latest replicated data manifest and writes a status file such as failover-status/run-0042_json. Test the procedure in a staging account before relying on it in production. Confirm that the role cannot write to any prefix other than failover-status/.
